I am a **Data Scientist, Software Developer, Bioinformatician, and Instructor** with over 20 years of software development and project management experience, as well as advanced biostatistics skills.

I am currently a PhD student in Health Data Science – Bioinformatics at George Washington University, with research interests in applying artificial intelligence to the analysis of genomic, metabolomic, microbiome, and other omics data. In my doctoral research, I am applying novel [genomic language models (gLMs)](research.qmd) to improve omics characterization over traditional, search-based techniques.

For the past eight years, I have been a sought-after health data science consultant and instructor both within and beyond GW. As an expert R and Python programmer, I practice and advocate for best practices in collaborative, open, and reproducible research — and I [teach](teaching.qmd) other researchers the fundamental data and computational skills they need to grow and succeed in their research.

## Highlights

- Co-author of two 2025 papers in JAMA journals on precision psychiatry and perinatal mental health — see [Publications](publications.qmd)
- Doctoral research benchmarking **genomic language models** for taxonomic and functional profiling in human microbiome multi-omics — see [Research & Projects](research.qmd)
- Certified [Carpentries](https://carpentries.org/) instructor; have organized and taught Data Carpentry workshops across the U.S. and internationally — see [Teaching](teaching.qmd)
- Developer of [Social Feed Manager](https://github.com/gwu-libraries/sfm-ui) and other open-source tools for researchers — see [Experience](experience.qmd)

## Education

- **Ph.D., Health Data Science – Bioinformatics**, George Washington University, expected 2028
- **M.S., Health and Biomedical Data Science – Applied Bioinformatics**, George Washington University, 2024
- **M.S., Systems Engineering**, University of Virginia, 1996
- **B.S., Applied and Engineering Physics**, Cornell University, 1994
